skill.name: conductor-revert
skill.description: Guides safe git revert workflows for Conductor tracks, phases, and tasks.
skill.summary: Plan and execute Conductor git reverts by logical work unit.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static Ruby backtick alerts are mostly Markdown inline code and fenced examples, not executable Ruby. I confirmed the findings that instruct agents to run git status, git log, git revert, or other git commands, and added semantic findings for unvalidated placeholder input and destructive rollback guidance. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: User-selected track, phase, and task values are shown inside shell command templates.
remediation.suggestion: Require strict identifier validation and use argv-style command execution instead of shell interpolation.

remediation.issue: The skill executes git commands that modify repository history.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the full plan display, require exact YES confirmation, and add a dry-run review step before any git revert.

remediation.issue: The undo guidance includes reset and checkout commands that can discard local work.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer reverting the revert commits, and move destructive alternatives behind stronger warnings and backup steps.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger static command alerts.
remediation.suggestion: Clearly label examples as commands the agent must not run until after validation and user confirmation.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.
- If missing: Display error and suggest running `/conductor:setup` first
- Run `git status` to confirm git repo
- In tracks.md: Ensure marked as `[~]` if partially complete, `[ ]` if fully reverted
2. **NEVER use `git push --force`** - Only safe push operations

content.value_statement: Git reversions can be hard to scope when work is grouped by tracks, phases, and tasks. This skill guides safe commit discovery, confirmation, git revert execution, and Conductor status updates.
actual_capabilities: Parses Conductor revert targets for full tracks, phases, and tasks.
Finds matching commits by track ID, task labels, and track directory history.
Displays a revert plan with commits, affected files, and plan updates.
Requires exact YES confirmation before revert execution.
Guides plan.md, metadata.json, and tracks.md status updates after reverts.
Handles merge conflicts by halting and presenting resolution options.
limitations: Depends on Conductor files and git history that follow expected naming patterns.
Can miss commits whose messages do not mention the track or task.
Does not resolve merge conflicts automatically.
Includes powerful git operations that require careful human review.

use_cases.title: Undo One Completed Task
use_cases.description: Identify the commits for a single Conductor task and prepare a scoped revert plan.

use_cases.title: Roll Back a Phase
use_cases.description: Review all task commits in one phase and reset related plan status after reversal.

use_cases.title: Reverse a Full Track
use_cases.description: Find every commit for a track and coordinate a full revert with clear warnings.

output_examples.output: The skill identifies task commits, lists affected files, explains plan status changes, and waits for exact YES before modifying the repository.

output: The skill groups matching task commits for the phase.
It shows which Conductor plan entries will return to pending.
It stops if conflicts appear and asks for manual resolution.

output_examples.input: Undo a revert that caused problems.
output_examples.output: The skill explains safer recovery choices first, warns about destructive alternatives, and recommends verification before continuing.

best_practices: Review the full revert plan before approving any repository changes.
Validate track, phase, and task identifiers before running git commands.
Run the project test suite and inspect Conductor status after completion.
anti_patterns: Approving a revert without checking the affected files and commits.
Using the undo guidance to discard local work without a backup.
Running this workflow outside a clean git repository.

faq.question: Does this skill use git reset hard?
faq.answer: No. The safety rules prohibit git reset hard and prefer git revert for history preservation.

faq.question: Can it revert a single task?
faq.answer: Yes. It accepts a track and task reference, then finds matching task and plan update commits.

faq.question: What happens if a merge conflict occurs?
faq.answer: The skill halts immediately, reports conflicted files, and asks for manual resolution or investigation.

faq.question: Does it update Conductor plan files?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides updates to plan.md, metadata.json, and tracks.md after successful reverts.

faq.question: Can it find every commit automatically?
faq.answer: Not always. It depends on commit messages and track paths that match the expected Conductor format.

faq.question: Is user confirmation required?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill requires the exact word YES before proceeding with revert operations.
